briefing:
Another week, another visionary decided to build their *own* personal AI assistant that runs locally and knows how *they* talk. Because the world truly needed AI fine-tuned on someone's internal monologue. Meanwhile, the enterprise side is still pushing the fantasy that AI will somehow rewrite our colossal fuck-ups into Rust and magically make things faster. Spoiler alert: bad design isn't a language problem, it's a 'we hired the cheapest engineers' problem. Some things are just fundamentally slow because they're stupid.

And speaking of basic things being absurdly complex, we've got fresh tutorials on building a 'reusable' contact form in React, complete with validation. Because apparently, `<form>` tags are too primitive now. All that effort, just for it to inevitably choke on a HEIC file from an iPhone, because of course it will. We're still fighting image format wars from 2005 while reinventing the most basic web components with enough layers to rival an onion.

Finally, for the old guard, the C die-hards are still out there insisting undefined behavior is totally fine, because 'we know what the code will do.' Yeah, just like those geniuses who apparently thought `return 4;` was perfectly random for a security-critical system. It’s truly incredible how many different ways we manage to trip over the same few bugs, year after year, all while calling it 'innovation.' Pass the coffee.

evidence.title: Why Your Image Upload Works With JPG but Fails With HEIC
evidence.facts:
• A profile-photo form works perfectly with your JPG test image.
• Then someone selects a photo from their iPhone, and the preview stays empty.
• The file may be perfectly valid.

evidence.title: Build a Reusable Contact Form in React with Validation
evidence.facts:
• Contact forms are common in React applications, but a good form needs more than a few input fields.
• It should manage user input, validate required fields, display helpful error messages, and prevent invalid submissions.
• In this tutorial, we'll build a reusable contact form using React functional components and the useState hook.

evidence.title: The glorious @xkcdRandom Zig builtin
evidence.facts:
• One of my favorite xkcd comics of all time is Random Number.
• The image depicts a C function that supposedly returns a random integer, but in reality always returns 4.
• I was reminded of this wonderful comic a few days ago, due to a security incident where people accidentally used the number 4 (among others) instead of a properly generated sequence of random bytes.

evidence.title: Software is slow because of bad design, not slow languages
evidence.facts:
• Many people are saying that AI will make software faster by rewriting it in faster languages, but this isn’t generally true.
• Most programs cannot be meaningfully sped up by rewriting them in C or Rust.
• How can this be true?
